narrative: Round 0 found real migration residue: five stale doc pointers, a stale FORKS.md caveat, and a deleted invariant enforcer. All were fixed correctly. Every later round reviewed the agent's own fixes: the completeness check moved into parsePolicy grew whitespace and padding gaps one round at a time, and the Unmarshal-to-Decoder swap for unknown keys dropped Unmarshal's trailing-content rejection. That trailing-content check had been promised in a reply and not shipped, so six round-3 findings repeated it. Each documentation fix also left a sibling statement unreconciled (dbsnapshot's lock order, policy.json's note, FORKS.md's 9-vs-10 count).
guidance_observations: The agent fixed each finding at the exact instance named and left the same class open, so policy.go was strictness-hardened across four rounds (blank, padded, trailing, duplicate, allowlist) instead of in one pass.

The plan reply for F9 promised a trailing-content check that the commit did not contain, which cost a full round of six duplicate findings; a 'Fixed in' reply should be checked against the plan's promises.
Two-document consistency findings (F20, F5) were fixed on only one side, so the next round flagged the other side.

evidence: Since Go's module-graph pruning, go.sum routinely carries h1: hashes for modules that have no require line in go.mod, so a mysql v1.10.0 hash without a require line does not by itself show untidiness. The packet shows neither go.mod nor a tidy run. This is a dependabot PR the agent never answered, and dependabot closed it as superseded.

This is the same claim as F1, about modernc.org/libc, modernc.org/sqlite and prometheus/procfs hashes. Whether `go mod tidy` would change go.sum cannot be determined from the packet, which has no go.mod and no tidy output. The PR was closed unmerged with no agent reply.

narrative: This is a dependabot group bump the agent never engaged with. The reviewer raised two go.sum tidiness advisories that rest on the questionable premise that every h1: hash needs a matching go.mod require line. Dependabot closed the PR as superseded, so neither thread was answered.
guidance_observations: Reviewer findings on bot-authored dependency PRs go unanswered, so a doubtful premise like go.sum tidiness is never contested or confirmed.
